sayfalar.t: accounting terms glossary IFRS accounting terminology definition example [Amount] recoverable The higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use. A mounts recognised (in the balance sheet and income statement) Amounts recorded in the financial statements. Accelerated depreciation allowances Tax rules allowing faster write-down of assets. Acceptable under IFRSs Describes an accounting treatment or presentation that complies with the requirements of International Financial Reporting Standards. Accountability of management Management's duty to account for its stewardship. Accounting The process of recording, classifying and summarising financial transactions. Accounting acquiree The entity whose accounting is treated as the acquiree in a reverse acquisition. Accounting and Reporting by Retirement Benefit Plans The standard that prescribes how retirement benefit plans report their obligations and plan assets to participants. Accounting arbitrage Exploiting differences between accounting rules to gain value. Accounting estimate An approximation of a monetary amount when no precise measurement is possible. Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance Standard on accounting for government grants and related disclosures. Accounting for inventories Measuring and reporting inventory at the lower of cost and net realisable value. Accounting for Investments in Associates The standard governing how an investor accounts for its significant influence investments in associates, normally using the equity method. Accounting for revenue and associated expenses Recognising revenue together with related expenses. Accounting income Profit measured under accounting rules rather than tax rules. Accounting mismatch An inconsistency arising when related assets and liabilities are measured on different bases. Accounting model The framework of measurement and recognition bases an entity applies when preparing its financial statements. Accounting period Period covered by financial statements, usually one year. Accounting policies The specific principles and bases an entity applies in preparing financial statements. Accrual accounting assumption Transactions are recorded when they occur, not when cash moves. Accumulated depreciation Total depreciation charged against an asset to date. Accumulated profit or loss The cumulative net earnings of an entity that have not been distributed as dividends or transferred to another reserve. Accumulating compensated absences Paid absences that accumulate for future use. Achieve comparability Making financial statements comparable across entities and periods. Acquired entity The business or entity whose control is obtained by the acquirer. Acquired goodwill The excess of the consideration transferred over the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired in a business combination. Acquired in a business combination Asset or liability obtained through a business combination. Acquiree The business or entity that the acquirer obtains control over. Acquirer The entity that obtains control of another entity. Acquisition A business combination where one entity obtains control of another. Acquisition date The date on which the acquirer effectively obtains control of the acquiree in a business combination. Acquisition method The method used to account for business combinations. Active market A market where transactions occur frequently enough to provide pricing. Active use Use of an asset in the production or supply of goods and services. Actively marketed Describes an asset that is being actively offered for sale in its present condition at a reasonable price. Actuarial assumptions Demographic and financial estimates used to measure benefit obligations. Actuarial gains and losses Changes in the present value of a defined benefit obligation from experience adjustments. Actuarial present value of promised retirement benefits Present value of promised pension benefits using actuarial assumptions. Actuarial valuation Valuation of benefit obligations using actuarial assumptions. Actuarial valuation method A projected technique used to measure defined benefit obligations by estimating future payments and discounting them to present value. Additional comparative information Extra prior-period information beyond the minimum. Additional consideration Extra payment transferred beyond the initial consideration in a transaction. Additional disclosure Supplementary information provided beyond the minimum required disclosures. Additional Exemptions for First-Time Adopters Optional reliefs that ease the transition to IFRS for entities applying the standards for the first time. Adjust for consolidation procedures Correcting figures to remove intragroup effects before consolidation. Adjusted fair value Fair value modified to reflect specific rights, restrictions or conditions. Adjusted weighted-average shares Weighted-average shares adjusted for dilutive potential shares. Adjusting event (after the balance sheet date) An event after the reporting date that requires adjustment. Adjusting event after the reporting period An event occurring after the reporting date that provides evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period and requires adjustment. Adjustment A change to a previously recorded amount. Administrative expenses Costs of running the entity not tied to production or selling. Admission fees Amounts charged for initial admission to a membership or service arrangement. Advance A payment made by a customer before goods or services are delivered, creating an obligation on the seller. Adverse economic consequences Negative financial effects arising from an event or decision. Adverse event An unfavourable occurrence that may give rise to a loss or liability. After-tax amount An amount net of income tax. Agency A relationship where one party acts on behalf of another. Aggregate A total amount obtained by adding together individual components or items. Aggregation Combining items into classes. Aggregation criteria Rules for grouping items that share similar characteristics for reporting. Agreement date The date on which the parties reach a binding agreement. Agreements for the construction of real estate Contracts to build real estate where revenue recognition depends on whether the agreement is treated as a sale of goods or a construction service. Agreements in progress Contracts still being negotiated or not yet completed. Agricultural activity Managing the biological transformation of living animals or plants for sale. Agricultural produce The harvested product of a biological asset. Agriculture The standard covering biological assets and agricultural produce. Allocation The process of assigning a cost, revenue or amount to different periods, assets or activities. Allocation method The method used to allocate an amount. Allowance A contra account reducing the carrying amount of an asset. Allowance account A contra account recording estimated reductions in the value of a receivable. Allowed alternative treatment An alternative accounting treatment that older standards permitted alongside the benchmark treatment. American share option Option that may be exercised at any time before expiry. Amortisation Systematic allocation of the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life. Amortisation method The method used to allocate a depreciable amount over useful life. Amortisation period The period over which an intangible asset is amortised. Amortised cost The amount at which a financial asset or liability is measured after adjusting for principal repayments, accumulated amortisation and impairment. Amortised cost of a financial asset or financial liability The amount measured using the effective interest method. Amortising interest rate swap A swap whose notional amount declines over its life. Amount of inventories The carrying amount of inventory recognised in the financial statements. Amount payable The monetary sum that an entity is obliged to pay, typically under a contract or liability. Amount per share Monetary value attributable to a single share. Amounts recognised [in the statement of financial position or in the statement of comprehensive income] Monetary amounts recorded in the financial statements under applicable standards.
